subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: Should Telegram inline callbacks be allowed to approve/deny only Telegram DM pairing requests, or also higher-scope device/browser pairing approvals that currently require `operator.admin`?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally separate `operator.pairing` from `operator.admin`; adding chat-originated buttons changes the approval trust boundary and cannot be chosen safely by repair automation.

options.title: Typed DM Pairing Buttons First
options.body: Add inline approve/deny callbacks only for Telegram DM pairing codes, with callback data bound to the pairing challenge and existing `operator.pairing` checks preserved.

options.title: Unify With Device Approval Cards
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader channel-aware device scope upgrade design in #92666 and design a shared approval-card contract before implementation.

options.title: Keep CLI Approval Only
options.body: Close or defer inline approval buttons if maintainers want pairing approval to remain a terminal/local-host trust ceremony.

recommendation.title: Typed DM Pairing Buttons First
recommendation.body: Add inline approve/deny callbacks only for Telegram DM pairing codes, with callback data bound to the pairing challenge and existing `operator.pairing` checks preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: The most specific current-main history signal is recent work on device-pair command/auth helpers and approval scope enforcement where the maintainer choice must be applied.
